title: McKinsey is making job applicants spar with a fake AI client
source_used: The Verge (full text), citing The Wall Street Journal
key_facts: McKinsey will have some entry-level candidates hold a 10-minute conversation with an AI simulation of a client during interviews, according to The Wall Street Journal.
The simulation aims to reflect 80% of scenarios consultants might meet day to day and is not meant to mimic an unhinged client.
The AI will not score candidates; humans in the room will assess them.
Testing starts this fall for undergraduates seeking business-analyst jobs in some North American offices.
The WSJ says hundreds of candidates may use it.
quote_evidence: Consulting firm McKinsey & Company is going to ask some entry-level candidates to have a 10-minute conversation with an AI simulation of a client as part of the interview process, according to The Wall Street Journal.
The AI won't score the candidates — humans will be in the room to assess the candidates.
why_it_matters_hint: AI is entering graduate hiring as a test scenario, with humans still doing the judging.
